Boards should map convergence points and dependencies, rehearse compound shocks, assign ownership and crisis decision rights, and fund targeted alternatives that preserve room to act.

institutions. A useful counterweight to the TNFD adopter numbers when assessing whether disclosure is actually
shifting capital.

articles.report_summary: Canada's major property and casualty insurers — including Intact Financial, TD Insurance, Wawanesa, and Definity — are urging homeowners to flood- and fire-proof their properties as climate-related claims surge, with home-insurance premiums rising approximately 6% last year. CEOs are publicly calling on Prime Minister Mark Carney to reprioritise climate risk in government policy, warning that the current economic focus on the oil sector is crowding out adaptation measures. For actuaries, this signals intensifying physical risk pricing pressure and potential systemic capacity constraints in Canadian wildfire and flood zones.

articles.report_summary: A UNCTAD statistical report (published April 7, 2026 via China's Economic Daily) finds that most current climate finance is not genuinely additional — much of it represents reclassified existing official development assistance, with only a handful of donor countries meeting the 0.7% GNI ODA baseline. The report identifies widespread double-counting of projects simultaneously classified as ODA and climate finance, abuse of climate-marker systems for non-climate projects, and a growing share of non-concessional (market-rate) loans that risk worsening recipient country debt burdens.

articles.report_summary: The Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS) has issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) awarding up to $75,000 for research that develops innovative actuarial approaches to climate risk, covering five tracks: perils and hazard climate change, actuarial practice integration, mitigation and adaptation investment, insurability and market structure, and risk transfer and climate-related capital. articles.report_summary: SCIPP (South Central Climate Resilience Forum) is hosting its 2026 Forum April 15–17 in San Antonio, TX, convening government, private sector, academia, and community groups from Arkansas, Kansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, and Texas — one of the most disaster-prone US regions, frequently hit by billion-dollar climate events with escalating costs. SCIPP also announced a new peer-reviewed journal article by its researchers on "A Climatology of Gridded Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature for the Southeastern United States" (AMS Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatic Change), directly relevant to heat-stress mortality risk modeling for insurance and pension actuaries.

appearances.summary: The World Bank argues that water investment is constrained by weak budget execution as well as insufficient funding. It identifies project preparation, procurement coordination and the fit between annual budgets and long-term plans as key problems, and recommends credible project pipelines and multi-year public investment planning.
appearances.title: Money on the Table Why Better Budget Planning IsKey to Fixing the Water Crisis

available_content.supporting_excerpt: The World Bank Group's 2024 report, Funding a Water-Secure Future, documents that water sector budget execution averaged only 72 percent between 2009 and 2020, meaning roughly 28 cents of every allocated dollar is never spent. Sub-Saharan Africa averages around 62 percent. In other words, countries are failing to close the financing gap while also leaving allocated money on the table. The cost is borne by people still without reliable access to clean water. Why Does the Money Stay on the Table?

enrichment.summary: Marine heat waves are supercharging damage caused by hurricanes and tropical cyclones across the globe, a new study found. Researchers looked at 1,600 tropical cyclones — the broader category of storms that includes hurricanes — that made landfall since 1981 and found those that went over the extra-hot water were more likely to intensify rapidly, a problem that’s becoming more frequent. This resulted in 60% more disasters that caused at least $1 billion in damage — adjusted for inflation — when they hit land, according to a study in Friday’s journal Science Advances.

articles.report_summary: A peer-reviewed study published in Science Advances found that marine heat waves are causing hurricanes and tropical cyclones to intensify more rapidly, resulting in 60% more billion-dollar-plus weather disasters since 1981. Marine heat waves affect more than half of landfalling tropical cyclones and are occurring closer to coastlines with increasing frequency. For insurance actuaries, this reinforces the urgency of updating catastrophe models to account for rapid intensification risk.

articles.report_summary: A new analysis from InsuranceERM finds that the growing talent shortage in the insurance and reinsurance sector has escalated into a strategic-level business risk, with firms struggling to recruit and retain staff with actuarial, risk management, and climate analytics expertise. articles.report_summary: The International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRI) at Columbia University reports that the equatorial Pacific is transitioning from declining La Nina conditions toward ENSO-neutral, with a 90% probability for March-May 2026. However, El Nino probabilities rise rapidly from May onward, reaching 72-80% by July-September 2026. For insurance and actuarial users, the IRI forecast provides critical forward-looking climate intelligence: the shift toward El Nino conditions in mid-2026 would alter tropical cyclone activity, drought, and flood risk patterns globally, requiring scenario updates in catastrophe models and catastrophe bond pricing.

The results describe climatic suitability for outbreaks, rather than predicting the outbreaks themselves, and support local health and land-use planning.

appearances.summary: WRI's analysis finds that one-quarter of global crop production is exposed to highly stressed or unreliable water supplies. enrichment.summary: LONDON / NEW YORK, April 8, 2026 — Physical climate risks are emerging as a significant concern for the global insurance sector, with potential implications for broader financial stability, according to a new report by the MSCI Institute. Rising Losses and Changing Risk Models The report notes that insured losses from natural catastrophes totaled about $107 billion in 2025, marking another year of elevated claims. A substantial share of these losses has been linked to so-called “secondary perils,” including floods, wildfires, and severe storms, rather than singular large-scale events.

articles.report_summary: A new MSCI Institute report (April 8, 2026) finds that physical climate risks are increasingly viewed as a systemic financial stability issue, not just an insurance sector concern. The report notes $107 billion in global insured nat cat losses in 2025, with secondary perils (floods, wildfires, severe storms) accounting for a growing share — challenging the traditional reliance on historical loss data for pricing. It flags that insurance availability is becoming a critical enabler (or barrier) for infrastructure project financing, and highlights parametric insurance as a growing complementary risk management tool.

articles.report_summary: A new WEF article (April 2026) examines how systemic risks — including climate change, cyber threats, and geopolitical instability — act as a hidden tax on economic growth, and how the insurance industry's expanding role can help build societal resilience before shocks occur. The article highlights advanced risk modelling, data analytics, and early-warning systems as tools insurers can deploy. For climate actuaries, the piece underscores the growing expectation that insurers will serve as shock absorbers and long-term resilience partners for governments and corporates alike.

articles.report_summary: The March 2026 ISSB update reveals a significant rebranding: the "BEES" (Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services) project has been officially renamed to "Nature-related Disclosures", expanding its scope beyond biodiversity to cover all natural-related risks and opportunities. The renamed project will serve as a targeted supplement to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, maintaining full compatibility with existing ISSB standards while aligning with TNFD, SASB, GRI, and ESRS frameworks to reduce duplicative corporate disclosures. ISSB discussed advancing the Nature-related Disclosures project toward a consultation draft, marking it as the next major standard-setting milestone after the IFRS S2 amendments.

Severe convective storm losses remained moderate despite elevated activity and no major peak-loss event occurred. Insurance covered an estimated 42% of total economic losses, well above the long-term average.
articles.title: Swiss Re Institute — First-half 2026 insured natural catastrophe losses

articles.report_summary: In the wake of recent severe weather events — including the US bomb cyclone and UK Storms Ingrid and Chandra — a critical gap in business interruption (BI) insurance coverage for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) has come into focus. Many SMEs that suffered days of forced closure found their claims denied or delayed, and with natural disaster losses reaching ~$131 billion in H1 2025 (only ~$80 billion insured), the uninsured gap exceeds Bahrain's GDP. Current BI policy terms are inadequate for modern climate volatility — a direct call for product innovation in the actuarial and underwriting community.

occurrences.anchor_text: Asking Better Questions on Nature: For Bank Chief Risk Officers and Risk Committees

report_fields.summary:
A TNFD guide produced with UNEP FI, structured around ten questions for bank chief risk officers and risk
committees to test exposure to nature-related financial risk across credit and investment portfolios, with the
headline quantification that pollinator decline alone puts up to USD 577 billion of annual global crop production at
risk. It positions nature loss as a systemic financial-stability issue to be handled inside mainstream risk
frameworks rather than as a disclosure exercise, and is the bank-CRO companion to TNFD's earlier CFO and
asset-owner editions. Relevant to actuaries working on nature-related financial risk and on agricultural credit and
crop exposures.
Caveat. Partial verification. The UNEP FI landing page carries “September 2026” only and there is no matching item in
the UNEP FI news listing. Third-party coverage (Sustainable Japan, 18 September 2026) corroborates a release around
17–18 September but also states only the month. Title, URL, content and month are confirmed; the day is approximate.

catastrophes, with six major events between June and August across Ontario and Quebec generating over

assumptions for urban flood.

report_fields.summary:
Three deliverables assessing the observational base underpinning climate services. In-situ networks supporting
the 55 Essential Climate Variables still depend heavily on short-term research projects, in-kind contributions or
volunteers, with material gaps across Africa, South America, Southeast Asia and the polar regions; satellite
observation covers 42 of the 55 ECVs, and a February 2026 survey of 33 climate experts found communication
with decision-makers, not data access or quality, the most-cited barrier to uptake. This is the observational-input
risk sitting underneath every catastrophe model and physical-risk scorecard — known geographic gaps and
funding fragility in the underlying networks are a source of parameter uncertainty that is rarely priced.

occurrences.anchor_text: Closing data gaps can help Pacific Islands adapt to sea level rise

report_fields.summary:
Sea level in much of the western tropical Pacific has risen 10–15 cm since 1993, close to or nearly twice the
global rate, yet only 15.6% of the combined land area of vulnerable atoll nations has LiDAR coverage, only about
three in ten residents of vulnerable coastal areas have ground measurements, and fewer than one in ten square
kilometres of nearshore reef and seabed has been surveyed at all. Tuvalu's 2019 survey captured roughly 500
km² of land, reef and lagoon in about 37 flying hours. Elevation and bathymetry data of this quality is the binding
constraint on credible SIDS flood and inundation models, and its absence is a first-order source of model
uncertainty in parametric and sovereign risk-pool pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: We can measure climate resilience. Why aren't we investing in it?

report_fields.summary:
Parag Khanna and WEF's Head of Climate Resilience argue the measurement barrier to adaptation finance has
been cleared — climate analytics now support credible avoided-loss quantification — yet mitigation still takes
over 90% of climate finance (USD 1.3 trillion in 2022) against roughly USD 68 billion a year for adaptation, and
only 9% of assessed companies are committing capital to adaptation against USD 1.47 trillion of identified
physical climate risk. The three proposed fixes (standardised resilience metrics, shared data architecture, and
market incentives including resilience-linked debt, blended finance and parametric triggers) map directly onto
actuarial territory.

Group of Twenty (G20)
Website: g20.org
The structural finding of this cycle. The 2026 United States presidency runs only four working groups — Trade,
Growth and Deregulation, Innovation, and Energy Abundance. There is no Sustainable Finance Working Group,
no climate or environment working group and no disaster risk reduction working group. The G20 climate and
sustainable finance workstream has effectively been stood down for 2026, and the Energy Abundance Ministerial
communiqué is the evidence.

Moody's argues P&C insurers and reinsurers cannot close the protection gap alone given capital and regulatory
constraints, and positions insurance-linked securities as the marginal capacity source. Alternative capital
reached a record USD 147 billion in H1 2026; H1 2026 cat bond issuance set a record of nearly USD 18 billion;
outstanding cat bond market size was USD 65.6 billion at end-Q2 2026. Moody's cites Hurricane Melissa
(October 2025), which caused an estimated USD 12.2 billion of damage in Jamaica — 54% of GDP — and
triggered a full payout on a World Bank-backed USD 150 million parametric cat bond.

report_fields.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
report_fields.summary:
OECD and the incoming Turkish COP31 presidency announced a partnership to help countries turn climate
commitments into practical policies, with tagged workstreams covering mitigation and net-zero transition,
adaptation and resilience, finance and investment for climate goals, biodiversity, and resource efficiency. It
matters as the earliest signal of what COP31 will push on adaptation finance, and because with the G20 climate
track stood down (see G20 above) the OECD–COP31 axis is now the main functioning multilateral channel.
Caveat. Partial verification. Title, date and workstream tags confirmed from page metadata; the announcement body text
did not render, so no figures, named deliverables or COP31 logistics could be extracted.

occurrences.anchor_text: STATEMENT: UN Secretary-General's Climate Summit Calls for Faster, Fairer Climate Action

report_fields.summary:
WRI's response to the UNSG Climate Summit, organised around keeping 1.5°C within reach, mobilising finance
for developing countries, and — new emphasis — advancing adaptation during climate overshoot. Germany
announced a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap to 2045; WRI cites a benefit-cost ratio of more than 10:1
over a decade for adaptation spending. The formal arrival of “adaptation under overshoot” in the multilateral
agenda is the signal for scenario designers: it legitimises planning around temporary exceedance of 1.5°C rather
than treating it as a tail case.

report_fields.summary:
Estimates 775,000 jobs from nature tourism and agribusiness in Colombia by 2035 against a government-
identified pipeline of more than USD 32 billion in green investment opportunities. The transition-risk figure of note
is that about 4.7 million workers, roughly 22.6% of the current workforce, will be directly affected by the climate
transition, in a labour market where around 55% of workers were informally employed as of June 2026. A
concrete just-transition exposure quantification for an emerging-market sovereign, relevant both to sovereign
transition-risk scenarios and to life and health portfolios exposed to informal-sector displacement.

report_fields.summary:
WEF/BCG analysis: 2.4 billion workers, 70% of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat, with nearly
19,000 heat-linked worker deaths and 23 million injuries annually and projected productivity losses of USD 2.4
trillion a year by 2030. The implementation gap is the actuarially interesting number — 80% of companies name
extreme heat a business threat but only 28% have piloted interventions. Bayer reports a 20% reduction in heat-
related incidents in North America and USD 3,000 in avoided medical and lost-time costs per prevented claim, a
usable data point for workers' compensation and group health pricing.

WMO was the most productive monitored organisation in the window, with six in-scope items. The State of Global
Water Resources 2025 is the most useful single publication of the fortnight for hydrological catastrophe
modelling, and the iClimateAction observation-chain reports document the funding fragility and geographic gaps
in the networks that every nat-cat model implicitly depends on.
Extreme heat is putting 2.4 billion workers at risk. Here's how 4 companies are responding
IN WINDOW 22 SEP 2026 RESEARCH CLIMATE AND HEALTH
WEF/BCG analysis: 2.4 billion workers, 70% of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat, with nearly
19,000 heat-linked worker deaths and 23 million injuries annually and projected productivity losses of USD 2.4
trillion a year by 2030. The implementation gap is the actuarially interesting number — 80% of companies name
extreme heat a business threat but only 28% have piloted interventions. Bayer reports a 20% reduction in heat-
related incidents in North America and USD 3,000 in avoided medical and lost-time costs per prevented claim, a
usable data point for workers' compensation and group health pricing.

report_fields.summary:
EPA finalised a rule eliminating carbon emission limits on fossil-fuel-fired power plants, the sector responsible for
roughly a quarter of US climate pollution and its second-largest emissions source. WRI puts fossil electricity's
health toll at tens of thousands of avoidable impacts and hundreds of billions of dollars in health costs annually,
separate from climate-disaster costs averaging USD 150 billion a year. Following EPA's February 2026 reversal
of its own authority to limit climate pollution, this is a material transition-risk and litigation-risk data point for US
utility and energy exposures, and a concrete argument for reweighting away from rapid-transition scenarios in
US-centric books.

occurrences.anchor_text: BMA to prioritise substance of parametric risk transfer over contractual form for new PSPI

report_fields.summary:
The Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter responding to feedback on its January 2026
consultation for a dedicated Parametric Special Purpose Insurer class supporting structured, fully collateralised
parametric risk transfer. The BMA will look to the substance of risk transfer rather than contractual form,
admitting contracts structured as reinsurance, derivatives or swaps provided statutory requirements are met;
existing SPIs may transition, and some may write both indemnity and parametric business case by case. An
amendment to the Insurance Act 1978 is being drafted for Q4 2026. The most consequential regulatory
development of the window for parametric and index-based climate covers.

occurrences.anchor_text: Seychelles: African Development Bank approves $34 million loan to strengthen public services, private sector growth and climate resilience

report_fields.summary:
A USD 34 million policy-based loan naming climate resilience as one of three objectives alongside public service
delivery and private sector growth. Seychelles is the canonical high-protection-gap sovereign — extreme
concentration of GDP in coastal tourism and fisheries — so the structure of climate conditionality in policy-based
lending to such states is worth tracking as a proxy for where contingent finance is being layered.
Caveat. The release gives no breakdown of the climate resilience allocation or the specific measures financed. Note also
a site inconsistency: the article resolves at URL suffix -96985 while AfDB site search returns -96998; both serve the same
text.

The 2026 World Trade Report, launched at the opening of the Public Forum, finds a strengthened multilateral
trading system could increase global GDP by roughly 3% or USD 3 trillion by 2050, while failure to modernise
could reduce global output by up to 10%. Climate content is thin — the environmental transition is named as one
of the forces reshaping trade but the report is not structured around climate. Retained because the macro-
fragmentation assumptions feed directly into the narrative layer of transition scenarios, and because
fragmentation is the same mechanism that constrains cross-border reinsurance capacity.

occurrences.anchor_text: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

report_fields.summary:
Documents a structural mismatch between policy incentive and buyer behaviour in the US voluntary market:
despite Section 45Q paying USD 180/t for direct air capture, DAC is only 2% of the largest US buyer's portfolio,
while biomass carbon removal and storage accounted for 96% of durable CDR purchase volume in 2025
(BECCS alone 69%). California's compliance programme has issued over 267 million offset credits through
2024, 81% from forest projects. The US CDR buyer base has doubled since 2022 to 69 buyers but average
purchase size has fallen — a thinning, not deepening, market.

occurrences.anchor_text: Zambezi Basin Countries Agree on Climate Resilience Priorities for $130 Million Program

report_fields.summary:
Eight riparian states — Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe —
agreed priorities for a USD 130 million regional resilience programme with the Zambezi Watercourse
Commission, structured around natural resources management, community climate resilience, institutional
capacity and coordination, and recommending members allocate at least 10% of national budgets to programme
priorities. The basin supports over 380 million people dependent on hydropower, agriculture, fisheries and
drinking water, making it one of the most concentrated transboundary drought and hydrological risks on the
continent and a natural candidate for regional index-based risk transfer.

Third in an FAO series on the livestock sector's contribution to food security and sustainable agrifood systems.
Livestock supplies a third of global protein and roughly 40% of agricultural GDP (about USD 1.8 trillion) while
contributing 12% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, cattle the largest share and enteric methane a
major source; emission profiles differ by system, with low-external-input systems emitting less per unit area and
high-input systems less per kilogram of output. Relevant to transition risk in agricultural lending and insurance
books, and a counterweight to blanket sectoral exclusion approaches.

to fund mulching, composting and crop diversification against shifted rainfall seasons. Included at the margin as
evidence of informal, community-level adaptation finance filling the segment that sits beneath the practical reach
of microinsurance and parametric products.

report_fields.summary:
Post-event analysis of the 26 August 2026 flood triggered when an ice-and-rock avalanche dammed a tributary
of the Bhotekoshi River on the Nepal–China border, with 1,300-plus confirmed dead and 5,000-plus missing
across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The central point for catastrophe modellers is that the hazard originated
in Tibet, outside Nepal's monitoring network, so no national early-warning system saw it coming — a
transboundary GLOF and landslide-dam blind spot that will recur across the Himalayas as glacial melt
accelerates.

of the Bhotekoshi River on the Nepal–China border, with 1,300-plus confirmed dead and 5,000-plus missing
across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The central point for catastrophe modellers is that the hazard originated
in Tibet, outside Nepal's monitoring network, so no national early-warning system saw it coming — a
transboundary GLOF and landslide-dam blind spot that will recur across the Himalayas as glacial melt
accelerates.
📎  Source: WEF stories, 24 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: What is the AO500? AlliedOffsets' carbon price index, explained

report_fields.summary:
Methodology note on the AO500, a retirement-weighted average price across the 500 highest-retirement-volume
carbon projects, built from over 17,000 price inputs a year and refreshed three times weekly; it closed at USD
6.30/t on 18 September 2026 against a 2026 range of USD 3.16–7.07 and a 2026 average to date of USD 6.04
(2024: USD 3.79). The companion Tradable20 index has averaged USD 2.58 below the AO500 in 2026. For
actuaries the AO500/Tradable20 spread is a direct, published measure of liquidity-tier basis risk in carbon-credit
valuation.

occurrences.anchor_text: Property reinsurance prices most likely to fall 7.5% to 15% in 2027: Moody's survey

report_fields.summary:
Moody's survey of reinsurance buyers points to property reinsurance prices falling 7.5–15% in 2027 following
double-digit reductions in 2026, with 86% expecting declines, up from 74% who expected declines for 2026 —
buyers having under-called the severity of the 2026 softening. A meaningful minority expect falls beyond 15%,
and 28% plan to increase their use of alternative capital in 2027. Relevant to anyone setting 2027 reinsurance
cost assumptions or modelling the cost of buying additional climate-driven catastrophe capacity.

report_fields.summary:
Kenya's mean temperature rose 0.27°C per decade over 2000–2024, faster than the global average; cooling
degree days are up 76% since 2000 to 793 in 2024; under high-emissions scenarios 95% of the electricity grid
faces up to 20% increases in heavy rainfall by mid-century; hydropower potential is projected to fall roughly 10%
through mid-century; sea level is rising 3.44 cm per decade with projections of 21–75 cm by 2100. Six hazard
categories are mapped onto specific energy assets — grid transmission capacity and generation efficiency, flood
and drought, Mombasa port and coastal infrastructure, mountain transmission landslides, wildfire, and
geothermal cooling water dependent on Lake Naivasha. This is the hazard-to-asset-performance chain actuaries
need for infrastructure and utility scenario analysis, and it is the first in a country series worth tracking.
report_fields.title: National Climate Resilience Assessment for Kenya

occurrences.anchor_text: New UN Climate Change tool strengthens tracking of non-Party climate action

report_fields.publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
report_fields.summary:
UNFCCC launched the Initiative Self-Service on the NAZCA portal, letting cooperative climate initiatives report
progress against a common framework with annual September submissions feeding the Yearbook of Global
Climate Action; more than 300 initiatives are registered, a 70% rise since 2018, with 190 actively reporting. The
relevance is transition-risk data quality: NAZCA is the principal public register of non-state commitments, and a
standardised self-reporting layer changes what evidence is available when assessing the credibility of a
counterparty's or portfolio company's pledge.

NGFS Annual Report 2025
IN WINDOW 16 SEP 2026 REPORT
Records NGFS membership at 170 members and observers across five continents at end-2025, names the
year's principal deliverables as the short-term climate scenarios for central banks and supervisors and an input
paper on integrating adaptation and resilience into transition plans, and reports a strategic tilt towards capacity
building and technical assistance. Confirms that adaptation and resilience finance has moved into the NGFS
core work programme, and serves as the authoritative baseline on what supervisory tooling members are
expected to have in hand.
Caveat. Date taken from the NGFS publications listing (16 September 2026); the detail page renders 24 September
2026 as a last-updated stamp, and no press release was issued to triangulate a third time. Both candidate dates sit
inside the window.
📎  Source: NGFS publications, 16 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: UN Climate Chief major keynote: thanks to global renewables, humanity avoided almost half a trillion US dollars in fossil fuel costs last year

report_fields.publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
report_fields.summary:
Simon Stiell's keynote to the Build Clean Now Industry Acceleration Summit in New York puts 2025 renewable
additions at 693 GW and avoided fossil-fuel cost at close to USD 500 billion, against clean-energy investment
now above USD 2 trillion a year, with 19 commercial-scale clean projects worth roughly USD 43 billion reaching
final investment decision in H1 2026. He restates the shift in the central warming projection from about 4°C to
2.6°C, the Baku-to-Belém USD 1.3 trillion mobilisation goal, and a target of electricity at 35% of global final
energy by 2035. The 2.6°C figure and the USD 1.3 trillion target are the reference points regulators and scenario
providers will anchor to.

Technical brief on climate advisory services delivered by SMS, app, USSD, voice, radio and helpline, arguing
that services designed on an assumption of equal farmer access amplify rather than reduce disparities, and that
advisories must be linked to the inputs farmers need to act on them. Directly relevant to index and parametric
agricultural insurance: advisory reach and trust determine whether climate information changes behaviour, which
bears on both basis risk and take-up assumptions in smallholder index products.
Caveat. No quantified usage or outcome statistics on the landing page.

occurrences.summary:
World Trade Organization (WTO)
Website: wto.org
The WTO produced the most consequential single development of the fortnight. On 25 September the Dispute
Settlement Body established a panel to review the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
Separately, the Public Forum ran 15–17 September in Geneva with more than 4,600 participants, and the World
Trade Report 2026 launched on 15 September. WTO content was retrieved this cycle through a browser session
on the bound device, which worked where automated fetching does not.

occurrences.anchor_text: 60% expect property cat rates to fall, 86% expect T&Cs to loosen: Fitch reinsurance survey

report_fields.summary:
Fitch finds 60% expect property catastrophe pricing to decline in 2027, a fifth of those by more than 10%, and
86% expect terms and conditions to loosen (58% selectively, 28% broadly). Fewer than 10% rank property or
property cat as a capital-allocation priority. Fitch's read is that persistent excess P&C capital will push
competition into terms-and-conditions erosion rather than headline rate — the more dangerous form of softening,
because loosened attachment points and hours clauses are not visible in rate indices.

report_fields.summary:
Technical brief framing climate risk assessment for electricity transmission and distribution networks and
integrating resilience measures across the project cycle, covering extreme heat, flooding, wildfire, landslide, and
sand and dust storms against network reliability, asset life and financial viability, with evidence from the
Mauritania–Mali Interconnection, Eastern Ethiopia Grid Reinforcement and Mozambique's Songo-Matambo. The
claimed cost–benefit evidence for adaptation spend is precisely the evidence base most often missing when
pricing resilience investment.
Caveat. Headline figures sit in the downloadable PDF; the landing page carries abstract-level text only.

report_fields.summary:
IEA flagship. Electricity demand grew over 3% a year in 2015–2025, twice the pace of overall energy demand;
EVs reached nearly 25% of new car sales in 2025 from under 1% in 2015; electricity is about 23% of total final
energy consumption. Under the High Electrification Scenario the global electrification rate reaches 35% by 2035,
with transport moving from 2% to 13%; HES paired with accelerated low-emissions generation cuts end-use
emissions 40% by 2035 and total energy-sector emissions by more than half from 2025 levels. Included on the
transition-risk test rather than as market commentary: it supplies scenario inputs (StePS versus HES) and
emissions trajectories usable directly in transition scenario analysis.

occurrences.anchor_text: Swiss Re highlights growing catastrophe protection gap as nat cat losses rise 5-7% annually

report_fields.summary:
Swiss Re puts structural trend growth in insured nat-cat losses at 5–7% a year, with European wildfire losses
compounding an estimated 8–11% annually over recent decades. Modelled insured losses could reach roughly
USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak-loss scenario, and a 2017-style hurricane cluster alone pushes annual insured
losses above USD 120 billion, against 2025 global insured nat-cat losses of USD 120 billion. The 5–7% trend
rate is the single most citable figure this fortnight for calibrating loss-trend assumptions in catastrophe pricing
and ORSA scenarios.

report_fields.summary:
The annual ozone bulletin reports the 2025 Antarctic ozone hole as the fourth-to-fifth smallest since severe
depletion was first observed in 1992, with full recovery expected within several decades, and records UV
radiation rising by as much as 20% in parts of Europe since the mid-1990s, driven mainly by reduced cloud
cover. Marginal but retained on two counts: the Kigali Amendment HFC phase-down is a live transition-risk
exposure for the cooling and refrigeration value chain, and the UV trend is a slow-burn morbidity signal for life
and health portfolios.

report_fields.summary:
Launch of the State of Global Water Resources 2025. 2025 was among the driest years for river discharge in
over 35 years, with below-normal flows across 36% of global basin area; for the seventh consecutive year basins
in normal condition were a minority at 34–38% against a 1991–2020 norm of 46%. Glaciers lost mass for a
fourth straight year across all regions, 1,400 gigatonnes over 2023–2025, and nearly two-thirds of monitored
groundwater wells sat outside historical norms. Asia and Africa accounted for at least 50% of water-related
extreme events and over 80% of associated deaths in the last five years. The headline finding — that the cycle
now oscillates between too little and too much rather than trending in one direction — directly degrades
stationarity assumptions in flood and drought models.
report_fields.title: WMO: Recent water trends have serious future implications

occurrences.summary:
Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
Website: oecd.org
Five in-window items in scope, headed by a policy brief on micro-disaster risk finance in Emerging Asia that is the
most directly actuarial OECD output in months. A steel transition paper and the Switzerland Economic Survey's
adaptation chapter add transition and physical-risk material respectively. OECD also announced a strategic
partnership with the incoming Turkish COP31 presidency.
Guide for supervisors: Integrating climate and nature-related risks into prudential supervision
IN WINDOW 21 SEP 2026 GUIDANCE SUPERVISION
The first full rewrite of the NGFS supervisory guide since 2020, walking supervisors through physical and
transition risk transmission, mandate relevance, strategy setting, exposure assessment and the deployment of
micro- and macroprudential tools on a progressive and proportionate basis, evidenced by a member survey
covering 70% of NGFS jurisdictions. For actuaries this is the clearest signal yet that protection-gap and nat-cat
concentration metrics are migrating out of insurance supervision and into bank prudential capital-setting, and
that nature risk is being put on the same supervisory footing as climate.
Caveat. Secondary reporting (Green Central Banking, 25 September 2026) states the guide contemplates capital buffers
for banks with concentrated exposure to climate-vulnerable regions or sectors, extra capital against large mortgage
books in flood-prone areas, LTV adjustments for green assets, and explicit supervisory monitoring of the insurance
protection gap for financial-stability purposes, and reports that about 40% of surveyed members currently consider
nature-related risks. Those four specifics are secondary-sourced: the 2.14 MB NGFS PDF was not opened, so they
should be confirmed against the primary text before being relied upon.
📎  Source: NGFS publications, 21 September 2026

report_fields.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
report_fields.summary:
OECD Policy Brief on closing the household and micro-enterprise protection gap in Emerging Asia, a region that
suffered USD 685 billion of disaster damage over 2010–2024, the large majority uninsured. It assesses
microinsurance and micro-catastrophe bonds as delivery mechanisms and concludes that community-level
exposure data and local risk knowledge are the binding constraint on product design — which is to say, on
pricing and basis risk in index-based micro-covers for a segment that is very thinly modelled.

The 85-member Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance published an updated Call to Action to Private Market Asset
Managers setting seven expectations of general partners across private equity, private debt, infrastructure and
real estate, including firm-level net-zero alignment, better financed-emissions data quality, engagement-led
decarbonisation and explicit integration of physical climate risk analysis, anchored on a principle of acting on
data available today rather than waiting for perfect data. Material for life and pension actuaries: private markets
are the segment where climate data is weakest and valuations least mark-to-market, and asset owners are now
setting explicit physical-risk expectations on general partners.

complete country architecture for disaster risk management. A Tunisia water-scarcity economic monitor and a

only: the World Bank's curated landing pages render no abstract, so no figures could be extracted from any of the
seven.

Inger Andersen's address to the 175th meeting of the Committee of Permanent Representatives in Nairobi. Two
quantified claims are worth carrying into scenario work as sensitivities around central warming pathways: full
implementation of the Kigali Amendment could avoid up to 0.5°C of warming by end-century, and deploying
available methane abatement across fossil fuel, agriculture and waste could avoid up to 0.2°C by 2050. These
are the figures UNEP will repeat into COP31.

occurrences.anchor_text: New roadmap signals Africa's pathway for sustainable and resilient agriculture

report_fields.summary:
Marking ten years of the Initiative for the Adaptation of African Agriculture, FAO released The State of African
Agricultural Adaptation, 2016–2026: Assessment and Roadmap to 2036. Forty-six of 53 African countries have
costed combined adaptation needs of USD 566 billion across national plans — about USD 56 billion a year — of
which at least USD 80 billion is specifically agricultural, and that is a floor because 22 countries have not
itemised agriculture separately. This is the most usable denominator published this fortnight for African
adaptation protection-gap and sovereign-risk work.
report_fields.title: New roadmap signals Africa's pathway for sustainable and resilient agriculture

occurrences.anchor_text: Busy August pushes Allstate's current aggregate year pre-tax cat losses to $3.15bn

report_fields.summary:
Allstate reported USD 748 million of pre-tax catastrophe losses in August 2026 from 21 separate events, half
from a single wind and hail occurrence, taking April–August aggregate pre-tax cat losses to USD 3.15 billion. Its
only current annual aggregate protection is the USD 150 million Class B tranche of Sanders Re III (Series 2023-
1), attaching at USD 4.78 billion with a USD 50 million per-event deductible, while a new USD 1 billion aggregate
excess-of-loss layer for 2026 attaches at USD 8.5 billion with a USD 1 million event deductible. A clean worked
illustration of how per-event deductibles inside aggregate structures create qualifying-loss uncertainty — a live
reserving and disclosure problem.
report_fields.title: Busy August pushes Allstate's current aggregate year pre-tax cat losses to $3.15bn

occurrences.anchor_text: As cat bond loss multiples tighten, AM Best urges investors towards greater selectivity

report_fields.summary:
AM Best reports cat bond loss multiples compressing to 2.5x in H1 2026 from 3.28x in H1 2025, with 2026 year-
to-date at 2.4x against 3.0x in 2025 and 3.71x in 2024. Weighted average spread fell 96 basis points while
expected loss on new issuance rose 30 basis points against H1 2025 — investors are being paid less for more
risk. Returns at 30 June 2026: Swiss Re Global Cat Bond Index 4.1%, ILS Advisers Index 3.9%. The
simultaneous fall in multiple and rise in expected loss is the sharpest risk-adjusted-return warning of the window
and bears directly on the cost and reliability of alternative capacity into the January 2027 renewals.

occurrences.anchor_text: ITU-WMO event to review risks to radio spectrum for weather and climate services

report_fields.summary:
Announcement of a joint ITU–WMO symposium on 28–30 September reviewing threats to the radio frequencies
underpinning weather forecasting, climate monitoring, water management and hazard early warning as demand
for wireless and satellite services accelerates. A non-obvious systemic dependency: degradation of protected
spectrum would directly reduce forecast skill and early-warning lead time, with knock-on effects for parametric
trigger reliability and catastrophe model input quality.

occurrences.anchor_text: Pacific ministers chart course for stronger weather and climate services

report_fields.summary:
The Fourth Pacific Meteorological Ministers Meeting in Nuku'alofa adopted the Siu-í-Álaimoana-Ki-Likutapu
Declaration committing to stronger National Meteorological and Hydrological Services and expanded multi-
hazard early warning, and advanced a Pacific Islands Meteorological Strategy 2027–2036. Tonga's Prime
Minister put the region's average annual cost of weather and climate events at half a billion US dollars, and the
meeting flagged El Niño conditions expected to peak between November 2026 and January 2027. Directly
relevant to Pacific disaster-risk-financing and parametric programme design, and to the early-warning cost–
benefit case underpinning resilience-linked pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: 2026 Forum of the Standing Committee on Finance — Financing Climate Action for Water Systems and the Ocean

report_fields.source_label: UNFCCC event page and 24 July 2026 notification
report_fields.summary:
The SCF's annual Forum ran 21–22 September in Sydney, hosted by Australia with Pacific Island countries and
the Philippines, followed by the 41st SCF meeting 23–25 September, covering barriers to financing, enabling
environments, financial instruments and delivery mechanisms, and drawing on submissions from 31
organisations and country groups. Water-sector adaptation finance is the thinnest-covered segment of the
protection-gap picture and SCF Forum output typically feeds the COP finance agenda.
Caveat. Held in-window; no Forum summary report had been published as at 28 September 2026. Webcasts of both
Forum days are posted.

occurrences.anchor_text: How climate action can reduce security risks in the Hindu Kush Himalaya

report_fields.summary:
The Hindu Kush Himalaya supplies water to over 240 million people in the region and nearly two billion
downstream across 16 countries. Glacial ice was lost 65% faster in the 2010s than in the previous decade, with
projected 80% volume loss by 2100 on current emissions; the 2022 South Asian heatwave affected over one
billion people and the 2022 Pakistan floods hit 33 million people with over USD 30 billion in damage. Relevant to
compound physical-risk and correlated-loss assessment — glacial lake outburst flood, riverine flood and heat —
across a transboundary exposure base with very thin insurance penetration.

report_fields.summary:
Hurricane Polo's intensification put the USD 175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric cat bond in
focus. The bond triggers on central pressure and location, requiring central pressure at or below 937 mb, with
payouts of 25% to 100% of principal by intensity and landfall location. Polo reached Category 5 with central
pressure as low as 892 mb while offshore, then weakened to 120 mph and 954 mb approaching Baja landfall,
making a trigger unlikely. A textbook illustration of parametric basis risk: peak intensity far inside the trigger
threshold, but in the wrong place at the wrong time.

occurrences.anchor_text: Panel to review EU carbon border adjustment mechanism and emissions trading scheme

report_fields.source_label: WTO Dispute Settlement Body news archive, 25 September 2026
report_fields.summary:
The Dispute Settlement Body agreed on 25 September to the Russian Federation's request for a panel to review
the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism package and an alleged export subsidy under the EU emissions
allowance trading scheme — the request having first been considered and blocked at the DSB meeting of 24
July 2026. This is the first time a carbon border measure will be adjudicated under WTO dispute settlement. For
actuaries the significance is twofold: it converts CBAM from a settled policy parameter into a contested one,
which widens the plausible range of carbon-price and border-adjustment assumptions in transition scenarios for
EU-exposed industrials; and it is the clearest instance yet of climate policy generating first-order international
liability risk. The panel's timetable is not yet published.
Caveat. The WTO news archive does not expose item-level permalinks; the dated archive page is therefore cited as the
source. Title and date were read directly from both the 2026 news index and the DSB archive in a browser session.

participants across 113 sessions. Climate-relevant sessions included “Powering climate action through services

corridors and African transport services, environmental services trade, circular services, critical minerals supply-
chain resilience, and Fisheries Subsidies Agreement implementation. No climate-specific WTO publication other
than the World Trade Report launched at the Forum.
Caveat. Session-level programme detail corroborated via the Geneva Environment Network Public Forum page.

occurrences.anchor_text: Urban Flood and Gully Erosion Risk Management in the Congo Basin

report_fields.summary:
Exemplar case study with the World Bank on investment programmes across the Congo River Basin, covering
urban resilience to flood and erosion hazards alongside infrastructure access, capacity building and emergency
response. Gully erosion is a material and poorly modelled loss driver in rapidly urbanising African cities, and this
is one of the few structured treatments of it in the adaptation literature.
Caveat. No numerical risk metrics on the landing page.

occurrences.anchor_text: COP31 Global Sustainable Insurance Summit to catalyze climate resilience across the economy

report_fields.summary:
UNEP and the Insurance Association of Türkiye will co-host the summit on 13–14 November 2026 at the
Insurance House, Antalya, during COP31, under the theme “The Climate Resilience Imperative”. The named
deliverable is the global launch of the PSI white paper From Vulnerability to Insurability: building resilient
communities and economies in an era of rising physical climate risk, with an agenda spanning insurability
valuation, resilient cities, MSME protection gaps, climate–nature linkages, climate-related health risk in
insurance, data gaps and low-carbon investment. This is the most directly actuarial scheduled publication on the
forward calendar and should be diarised for November.

report_fields.summary:

adaptation financing need at USD 0.5–1.3 trillion by 2030. Sub-markets include climate-resilient construction at
USD 220–260 billion today growing 6–8% a year to USD 330–370 billion by 2030. The demand-side counterpart
to the resilience-metrics piece when building the investment case for adaptation-linked insurance products.

occurrences.anchor_text: Why circularity needs to be at the heart of industrial decarbonization

report_fields.summary:
Resource extraction and processing accounted for more than 55% of global emissions in 2022 and could rise
almost 60% from 2020 levels by 2060 absent intervention, while only 6.9% of raw materials currently cycle back
into the economy after first use; over 90% of third-generation NDCs name industry as a priority mitigation sector.
Material-efficiency pathways change the abatement cost curve, and therefore the plausibility of the industrial
decarbonisation assumptions embedded in climate scenario analysis for heavy-industry credit and equity
exposures.

occurrences.summary:
World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
Website: wmo.int
WMO was the most productive monitored organisation in the window, with six in-scope items. The State of Global
Water Resources 2025 is the most useful single publication of the fortnight for hydrological catastrophe
modelling, and the iClimateAction observation-chain reports document the funding fragility and geographic gaps
in the networks that every nat-cat model implicitly depends on.
Extreme heat is putting 2.4 billion workers at risk. Here's how 4 companies are responding
IN WINDOW 22 SEP 2026 RESEARCH CLIMATE AND HEALTH
WEF/BCG analysis: 2.4 billion workers, 70% of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat, with nearly
19,000 heat-linked worker deaths and 23 million injuries annually and projected productivity losses of USD 2.4
trillion a year by 2030. The implementation gap is the actuarially interesting number — 80% of companies name
extreme heat a business threat but only 28% have piloted interventions. Bayer reports a 20% reduction in heat-
related incidents in North America and USD 3,000 in avoided medical and lost-time costs per prevented claim, a
usable data point for workers' compensation and group health pricing.
📎  Source: WEF stories, 22 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: Navigating the Steel Transition amid Global Excess Capacity

report_fields.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
report_fields.summary:
OECD Science, Technology and Industry Policy Paper on how steel overcapacity blocks decarbonisation:
excess capacity depresses prices, squeezes margins, increases earnings volatility and borrowing costs, and
limits internal financing for technology deployment, while raising the relative price premium of low-emission steel
and weakening the demand signal. It warns that badly designed low-emission subsidies may themselves trigger
new waves of excess capacity. Opened and confirmed as a transition-risk paper rather than a trade paper;
directly relevant to credit and equity exposure to hard-to-abate industrials.

Marsh Re reports a 50% increase in traded limits for property aggregate excess-of-loss, with nearly 40% of
buyers now building frequency protection into excess-of-loss strategies, up from just over 25% two years ago;
property retro quota share limits placed exceed USD 20 billion, up 30% over four years. The return of aggregate
and frequency cover is the market's direct response to secondary-peril loss frequency — the structural feature
that had been priced out after 2022 — and it changes the shape of the protection available for climate-driven
attritional loss.

report_fields.summary:
The 2026 Status Report records over 1,000 organisations across 56 countries publishing TNFD-aligned
disclosures, a 100% year-on-year increase, with 802 committed Adopters and USD 26.6 trillion of AUM
represented by financial-institution adopters; 100 organisations have filed third-generation reports. Survey
findings material to insurers and asset owners: every investor surveyed is concerned about nature loss affecting
financial markets, 59% rank nature in their top three sustainability issues, 74% expect a two- to fivefold increase
in nature-related financing within five years, and over 70% support mandatory nature-related reporting. This is
now the baseline dataset for arguing nature-risk materiality to boards and supervisors.

At the Global Cooling Pledge Assembly in Singapore UNEP launched a Global Roadmap on Heat Resilience
covering schools, hospitals and energy systems, a Manufacturing Platform for efficient low-GWP equipment, and
the inaugural Cool Leaders awards; Brazil, Cambodia and Côte d'Ivoire launched a Nature for Cooling Challenge
backed by a USD 3 million GEF grant plus USD 33 million co-financing, targeting nature-based cooling that can
cut peak summer temperatures by up to 5°C. Global air-conditioner demand is projected to reach 5.6 billion units
by 2050, nearly triple today's level. Direct read-across to heat mortality and morbidity assumptions in life and
health portfolios, to heat-driven business interruption, and to the electricity-demand and HFC transition
exposures in the cooling value chain.
report_fields.title: Cool Leaders, a roadmap and nature for cooling: Global Cooling Pledge acts on heat

report_fields.summary:
CatIQ tallies over CAD 1.8 billion of insured losses from ten extreme weather events across Alberta,
Saskatchewan and Manitoba in summer 2026, the 9–10 June Saskatchewan/Manitoba severe storms alone at
CAD 900 million. Notably, flooding displaced the usual hail and wind as the dominant Prairie peril, with record
June and July rainfall in Edmonton. Insurance Bureau of Canada context: insured extreme-weather losses are
up roughly 320% since the late 1990s, with 2024 a record CAD 9.4 billion. A peril-mix shift of this kind is a direct
challenge to the hazard weights in Canadian property models.

that sits beneath regional parametric cover in a Pacific risk-financing stack.

report_fields.summary:
Quantifies the nature finance misalignment: USD 7.3 trillion flowed to nature-negative activities in 2023 against
USD 220 billion to nature-based solutions, a 30:1 ratio, with USD 22 billion a year in harmful fishing subsidies
prior to the 2025 WTO agreement. Argues capital alone is insufficient without redesigned incentives and
institutions. A useful counterweight to the TNFD adopter numbers when assessing whether disclosure is actually
shifting capital.

International Monetary Fund (IMF)
Website: imf.org
National Climate Resilience Assessment for Kenya
IN WINDOW 25 SEP 2026 REPORT PHYSICAL RISK
Kenya's mean temperature rose 0.27°C per decade over 2000–2024, faster than the global average; cooling
degree days are up 76% since 2000 to 793 in 2024; under high-emissions scenarios 95% of the electricity grid
faces up to 20% increases in heavy rainfall by mid-century; hydropower potential is projected to fall roughly 10%
through mid-century; sea level is rising 3.44 cm per decade with projections of 21–75 cm by 2100. Six hazard
categories are mapped onto specific energy assets — grid transmission capacity and generation efficiency, flood
and drought, Mombasa port and coastal infrastructure, mountain transmission landslides, wildfire, and
geothermal cooling water dependent on Lake Naivasha. This is the hazard-to-asset-performance chain actuaries
need for infrastructure and utility scenario analysis, and it is the first in a country series worth tracking.
📎  Source: IEA reports, 25 September 2026

almost entirely by landfall location. Against an estimated USD 148 billion of global insured cat losses in a normal
2026, an extreme Florida event would take the annual total past USD 450 billion. Directly usable for tail-scenario
and capital-adequacy stress testing.

occurrences.anchor_text: G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Chair's Statement

report_fields.summary:
Output of the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial held in Houston 14–16 September, structured around
affordability, supply expansion, diversification, infrastructure and resilience, and innovation. Climate language is
close to absent: the only emissions reference is a neutral list item naming “conventional sources and zero and
low emissions technologies”, with no mention of climate change, decarbonisation targets or climate finance.
Included deliberately, because for transition-risk purposes the absence is the signal — a G20 energy
communiqué stripped of emissions language, combined with the abolition of the Sustainable Finance Working
Group, lowers the probability weight on rapid-transition scenarios and raises it on delayed-and-disorderly and
hot-house pathways. That is a direct input to scenario selection in climate stress testing.

only: the World Bank's curated landing pages render no abstract, so no figures could be extracted from any of the
seven.

report_fields.summary:
CatIQ tallies over CAD 1.8 billion of insured losses from ten extreme weather events across Alberta,
Saskatchewan and Manitoba in summer 2026, the 9–10 June Saskatchewan/Manitoba severe storms alone at

occurrences.anchor_text: Cool Leaders, a roadmap and nature for cooling: Global Cooling Pledge acts on heat

report_fields.summary:
At the Global Cooling Pledge Assembly in Singapore UNEP launched a Global Roadmap on Heat Resilience
covering schools, hospitals and energy systems, a Manufacturing Platform for efficient low-GWP equipment, and
the inaugural Cool Leaders awards; Brazil, Cambodia and Côte d'Ivoire launched a Nature for Cooling Challenge
backed by a USD 3 million GEF grant plus USD 33 million co-financing, targeting nature-based cooling that can
cut peak summer temperatures by up to 5°C. Global air-conditioner demand is projected to reach 5.6 billion units
by 2050, nearly triple today's level. Direct read-across to heat mortality and morbidity assumptions in life and
health portfolios, to heat-driven business interruption, and to the electricity-demand and HFC transition
exposures in the cooling value chain.

occurrences.anchor_text: Climate Adaptation Investment Planning Lessons Series No. 1 to 3

report_fields.summary:
Three linked notes drawing on Armenia, Bhutan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Mongolia and Nepal: strategic climate
diagnostics to identify priority risks (No. 1), economic, fiscal and financial analysis to build the investment case
(No. 2), and financial matchmaking to connect investment packages to financing sources (No. 3). The middle
note is the technically significant one — it is an applied method for valuing avoided climate loss, which is the
same quantity a catastrophe model produces, and therefore the bridge between adaptation appraisal and
insurance pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: Property aggregate XoL rebounds with 50% increase in traded limits: Marsh Re

report_fields.summary:
Marsh Re reports a 50% increase in traded limits for property aggregate excess-of-loss, with nearly 40% of
buyers now building frequency protection into excess-of-loss strategies, up from just over 25% two years ago;
property retro quota share limits placed exceed USD 20 billion, up 30% over four years. The return of aggregate
and frequency cover is the market's direct response to secondary-peril loss frequency — the structural feature
that had been priced out after 2022 — and it changes the shape of the protection available for climate-driven
attritional loss.

report_fields.summary:
OECD Science, Technology and Industry Policy Paper on how steel overcapacity blocks decarbonisation:
excess capacity depresses prices, squeezes margins, increases earnings volatility and borrowing costs, and
limits internal financing for technology deployment, while raising the relative price premium of low-emission steel
and weakening the demand signal. It warns that badly designed low-emission subsidies may themselves trigger
new waves of excess capacity. Opened and confirmed as a transition-risk paper rather than a trade paper;
directly relevant to credit and equity exposure to hard-to-abate industrials.

occurrences.anchor_text: RELEASE: Global Forest Watch Becomes Global Nature Watch, Expanding to Cover More Land Ecosystems

report_fields.summary:
WRI rebranded and expanded Global Forest Watch — which monitors over 600 million hectares of forest and
has served more than 9 million users from 170-plus countries since 2014 — into Global Nature Watch, extending
near-real-time alerting beyond forests to grasslands and other vegetated ecosystems, with greenhouse gas
dynamics to follow, and a preview AI and geospatial interface called Horizon. Free, near-real-time ecosystem-
change data that can underpin TNFD LEAP location assessments and nature-related exposure screening at
portfolio level.

occurrences.summary:
World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
Website: wmo.int
WMO was the most productive monitored organisation in the window, with six in-scope items. The State of Global
Water Resources 2025 is the most useful single publication of the fortnight for hydrological catastrophe
modelling, and the iClimateAction observation-chain reports document the funding fragility and geographic gaps
in the networks that every nat-cat model implicitly depends on.
Extreme heat is putting 2.4 billion workers at risk. Here's how 4 companies are responding
IN WINDOW 22 SEP 2026 RESEARCH CLIMATE AND HEALTH
WEF/BCG analysis: 2.4 billion workers, 70% of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat, with nearly
19,000 heat-linked worker deaths and 23 million injuries annually and projected productivity losses of USD 2.4
trillion a year by 2030. The implementation gap is the actuarially interesting number — 80% of companies name
extreme heat a business threat but only 28% have piloted interventions. Bayer reports a 20% reduction in heat-
related incidents in North America and USD 3,000 in avoided medical and lost-time costs per prevented claim, a
usable data point for workers' compensation and group health pricing.
📎  Source: WEF stories, 22 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: The Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Strengthens Global Board Representation by Appointing Three New Directors

report_fields.summary:
PCAF appointed Neil Atkinson (Riyad Bank), José Luis Muñoz (Grupo Financiero Banorte) and Dafina
Nonkulovska (Rabobank) to its board, explicitly to widen emerging-market representation in the governance of
the Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard. Borderline for this report as governance rather than
methodology, but included because board composition steers the 2026–2028 standard agenda, two of whose
seven priority topics are new insurance methodologies — insurance claims, and personal non-life insurance —
which will determine how non-life insurers are expected to account for underwriting emissions.

occurrences.anchor_text: WTO Dispute Settlement Body news archive, 25 September 2026

report_fields.source_label: WTO Dispute Settlement Body news archive, 25 September 2026
report_fields.summary:
The Dispute Settlement Body agreed on 25 September to the Russian Federation's request for a panel to review
the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism package and an alleged export subsidy under the EU emissions
allowance trading scheme — the request having first been considered and blocked at the DSB meeting of 24
July 2026. This is the first time a carbon border measure will be adjudicated under WTO dispute settlement. For
actuaries the significance is twofold: it converts CBAM from a settled policy parameter into a contested one,
which widens the plausible range of carbon-price and border-adjustment assumptions in transition scenarios for
EU-exposed industrials; and it is the clearest instance yet of climate policy generating first-order international
liability risk. The panel's timetable is not yet published.
Caveat. The WTO news archive does not expose item-level permalinks; the dated archive page is therefore cited as the
source. Title and date were read directly from both the 2026 news index and the DSB archive in a browser session.

occurrences.anchor_text: Strengthening Hurricane Polo brings Mexico catastrophe bond into focus

report_fields.summary:
Hurricane Polo's intensification put the USD 175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric cat bond in
focus. The bond triggers on central pressure and location, requiring central pressure at or below 937 mb, with
payouts of 25% to 100% of principal by intensity and landfall location. Polo reached Category 5 with central
pressure as low as 892 mb while offshore, then weakened to 120 mph and 954 mb approaching Baja landfall,
making a trigger unlikely. A textbook illustration of parametric basis risk: peak intensity far inside the trigger
threshold, but in the wrong place at the wrong time.

The Hindu Kush Himalaya supplies water to over 240 million people in the region and nearly two billion
downstream across 16 countries. Glacial ice was lost 65% faster in the 2010s than in the previous decade, with
projected 80% volume loss by 2100 on current emissions; the 2022 South Asian heatwave affected over one
billion people and the 2022 Pakistan floods hit 33 million people with over USD 30 billion in damage. Relevant to
compound physical-risk and correlated-loss assessment — glacial lake outburst flood, riverine flood and heat —
across a transboundary exposure base with very thin insurance penetration.

The Fourth Pacific Meteorological Ministers Meeting in Nuku'alofa adopted the Siu-í-Álaimoana-Ki-Likutapu
Declaration committing to stronger National Meteorological and Hydrological Services and expanded multi-
hazard early warning, and advanced a Pacific Islands Meteorological Strategy 2027–2036. Tonga's Prime
Minister put the region's average annual cost of weather and climate events at half a billion US dollars, and the
meeting flagged El Niño conditions expected to peak between November 2026 and January 2027. Directly
relevant to Pacific disaster-risk-financing and parametric programme design, and to the early-warning cost–
benefit case underpinning resilience-linked pricing.

AM Best reports cat bond loss multiples compressing to 2.5x in H1 2026 from 3.28x in H1 2025, with 2026 year-
to-date at 2.4x against 3.0x in 2025 and 3.71x in 2024. Weighted average spread fell 96 basis points while

Allstate reported USD 748 million of pre-tax catastrophe losses in August 2026 from 21 separate events, half
from a single wind and hail occurrence, taking April–August aggregate pre-tax cat losses to USD 3.15 billion. Its
only current annual aggregate protection is the USD 150 million Class B tranche of Sanders Re III (Series 2023-
1), attaching at USD 4.78 billion with a USD 50 million per-event deductible, while a new USD 1 billion aggregate
excess-of-loss layer for 2026 attaches at USD 8.5 billion with a USD 1 million event deductible. A clean worked
illustration of how per-event deductibles inside aggregate structures create qualifying-loss uncertainty — a live
reserving and disclosure problem.

occurrences.anchor_text: Guide for supervisors: Integrating climate and nature-related risks into prudential supervision

report_fields.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
report_fields.summary:
The first full rewrite of the NGFS supervisory guide since 2020, walking supervisors through physical and
transition risk transmission, mandate relevance, strategy setting, exposure assessment and the deployment of
micro- and macroprudential tools on a progressive and proportionate basis, evidenced by a member survey
covering 70% of NGFS jurisdictions. For actuaries this is the clearest signal yet that protection-gap and nat-cat
concentration metrics are migrating out of insurance supervision and into bank prudential capital-setting, and
that nature risk is being put on the same supervisory footing as climate.
Caveat. Secondary reporting (Green Central Banking, 25 September 2026) states the guide contemplates capital buffers
for banks with concentrated exposure to climate-vulnerable regions or sectors, extra capital against large mortgage
books in flood-prone areas, LTV adjustments for green assets, and explicit supervisory monitoring of the insurance
protection gap for financial-stability purposes, and reports that about 40% of surveyed members currently consider
nature-related risks. Those four specifics are secondary-sourced: the 2.14 MB NGFS PDF was not opened, so they
should be confirmed against the primary text before being relied upon.
report_fields.title: Guide for supervisors: Integrating climate and nature-related risks into prudential supervision

Website: artemis.bm

occurrences.anchor_text: NZAOA calls on private market asset managers to turn climate ambition into everyday practice

report_fields.summary:
The 85-member Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance published an updated Call to Action to Private Market Asset
Managers setting seven expectations of general partners across private equity, private debt, infrastructure and
real estate, including firm-level net-zero alignment, better financed-emissions data quality, engagement-led
decarbonisation and explicit integration of physical climate risk analysis, anchored on a principle of acting on
data available today rather than waiting for perfect data. Material for life and pension actuaries: private markets
are the segment where climate data is weakest and valuations least mark-to-market, and asset owners are now
setting explicit physical-risk expectations on general partners.

suffered USD 685 billion of disaster damage over 2010–2024, the large majority uninsured. It assesses
microinsurance and micro-catastrophe bonds as delivery mechanisms and concludes that community-level
exposure data and local risk knowledge are the binding constraint on product design — which is to say, on
pricing and basis risk in index-based micro-covers for a segment that is very thinly modelled.

occurrences.anchor_text: WMO: Recent water trends have serious future implications

report_fields.summary:
Launch of the State of Global Water Resources 2025. 2025 was among the driest years for river discharge in
over 35 years, with below-normal flows across 36% of global basin area; for the seventh consecutive year basins
in normal condition were a minority at 34–38% against a 1991–2020 norm of 46%. Glaciers lost mass for a
fourth straight year across all regions, 1,400 gigatonnes over 2023–2025, and nearly two-thirds of monitored
groundwater wells sat outside historical norms. Asia and Africa accounted for at least 50% of water-related
extreme events and over 80% of associated deaths in the last five years. The headline finding — that the cycle
now oscillates between too little and too much rather than trending in one direction — directly degrades
stationarity assumptions in flood and drought models.

report_fields.summary:
The annual ozone bulletin reports the 2025 Antarctic ozone hole as the fourth-to-fifth smallest since severe
depletion was first observed in 1992, with full recovery expected within several decades, and records UV
radiation rising by as much as 20% in parts of Europe since the mid-1990s, driven mainly by reduced cloud
cover. Marginal but retained on two counts: the Kigali Amendment HFC phase-down is a live transition-risk
exposure for the cooling and refrigeration value chain, and the UV trend is a slow-burn morbidity signal for life
and health portfolios.

Swiss Re puts structural trend growth in insured nat-cat losses at 5–7% a year, with European wildfire losses
compounding an estimated 8–11% annually over recent decades. Modelled insured losses could reach roughly
USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak-loss scenario, and a 2017-style hurricane cluster alone pushes annual insured
losses above USD 120 billion, against 2025 global insured nat-cat losses of USD 120 billion. The 5–7% trend
rate is the single most citable figure this fortnight for calibrating loss-trend assumptions in catastrophe pricing
and ORSA scenarios.

USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak-loss scenario, and a 2017-style hurricane cluster alone pushes annual insured
losses above USD 120 billion, against 2025 global insured nat-cat losses of USD 120 billion. The 5–7% trend
rate is the single most citable figure this fortnight for calibrating loss-trend assumptions in catastrophe pricing
and ORSA scenarios.
📎  Source: Artemis, 14 September 2026

competition into terms-and-conditions erosion rather than headline rate — the more dangerous form of softening,
because loosened attachment points and hours clauses are not visible in rate indices.

report_fields.summary:
Technical brief on climate advisory services delivered by SMS, app, USSD, voice, radio and helpline, arguing
that services designed on an assumption of equal farmer access amplify rather than reduce disparities, and that
advisories must be linked to the inputs farmers need to act on them. Directly relevant to index and parametric
agricultural insurance: advisory reach and trust determine whether climate information changes behaviour, which
bears on both basis risk and take-up assumptions in smallholder index products.
Caveat. No quantified usage or outcome statistics on the landing page.

report_fields.summary:
Simon Stiell's keynote to the Build Clean Now Industry Acceleration Summit in New York puts 2025 renewable
additions at 693 GW and avoided fossil-fuel cost at close to USD 500 billion, against clean-energy investment
now above USD 2 trillion a year, with 19 commercial-scale clean projects worth roughly USD 43 billion reaching
final investment decision in H1 2026. He restates the shift in the central warming projection from about 4°C to
2.6°C, the Baku-to-Belém USD 1.3 trillion mobilisation goal, and a target of electricity at 35% of global final
energy by 2035. The 2.6°C figure and the USD 1.3 trillion target are the reference points regulators and scenario
providers will anchor to.

counterparty's or portfolio company's pledge.

occurrences.anchor_text: National Climate Resilience Assessment for Kenya

report_fields.summary:
Kenya's mean temperature rose 0.27°C per decade over 2000–2024, faster than the global average; cooling
degree days are up 76% since 2000 to 793 in 2024; under high-emissions scenarios 95% of the electricity grid
faces up to 20% increases in heavy rainfall by mid-century; hydropower potential is projected to fall roughly 10%
through mid-century; sea level is rising 3.44 cm per decade with projections of 21–75 cm by 2100. Six hazard
categories are mapped onto specific energy assets — grid transmission capacity and generation efficiency, flood
and drought, Mombasa port and coastal infrastructure, mountain transmission landslides, wildfire, and
geothermal cooling water dependent on Lake Naivasha. This is the hazard-to-asset-performance chain actuaries
need for infrastructure and utility scenario analysis, and it is the first in a country series worth tracking.
report_fields.title: National Climate Resilience Assessment for Kenya

double-digit reductions in 2026, with 86% expecting declines, up from 74% who expected declines for 2026 —

cost assumptions or modelling the cost of buying additional climate-driven catastrophe capacity.

IN WINDOW 16 SEP 2026 RESEARCH REINSURANCE
Moody's survey of reinsurance buyers points to property reinsurance prices falling 7.5–15% in 2027 following
double-digit reductions in 2026, with 86% expecting declines, up from 74% who expected declines for 2026 —
buyers having under-called the severity of the 2026 softening. A meaningful minority expect falls beyond 15%,
and 28% plan to increase their use of alternative capital in 2027. Relevant to anyone setting 2027 reinsurance
cost assumptions or modelling the cost of buying additional climate-driven catastrophe capacity.
📎  Source: Artemis, 16 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: Exploring Premium Support in the Pacific

report_fields.summary:
ADB Briefs No. 405, on using a Multi-Donor Trust Fund to subsidise disaster insurance premiums for Pacific
island states that cannot finance them unaided, working through eligibility criteria, equal-allocation versus risk-
based allocation, and multiyear premium agreements, and insisting premium support be embedded in a full
disaster risk financing strategy rather than run as a standalone subsidy. Squarely actuarial: premium subsidy
design drives take-up, adverse selection and the long-run solvency of Pacific regional risk pools.
report_fields.title: Exploring Premium Support in the Pacific

occurrences.anchor_text: What is the AO500? AlliedOffsets' carbon price index, explained

report_fields.summary:
Methodology note on the AO500, a retirement-weighted average price across the 500 highest-retirement-volume
carbon projects, built from over 17,000 price inputs a year and refreshed three times weekly; it closed at USD
6.30/t on 18 September 2026 against a 2026 range of USD 3.16–7.07 and a 2026 average to date of USD 6.04
(2024: USD 3.79). The companion Tradable20 index has averaged USD 2.58 below the AO500 in 2026. For
actuaries the AO500/Tradable20 spread is a direct, published measure of liquidity-tier basis risk in carbon-credit
valuation.

occurrences.anchor_text: 4 lessons from young people on the frontlines of the Nepal-Tibet floods

report_fields.summary:
Post-event analysis of the 26 August 2026 flood triggered when an ice-and-rock avalanche dammed a tributary
of the Bhotekoshi River on the Nepal–China border, with 1,300-plus confirmed dead and 5,000-plus missing
across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The central point for catastrophe modellers is that the hazard originated
in Tibet, outside Nepal's monitoring network, so no national early-warning system saw it coming — a
transboundary GLOF and landslide-dam blind spot that will recur across the Himalayas as glacial melt
accelerates.
report_fields.title: 4 lessons from young people on the frontlines of the Nepal-Tibet floods

occurrences.anchor_text: New FAO report surveys how different livestock production systems can contribute to social, economic and environmental sustainability

report_fields.summary:
Third in an FAO series on the livestock sector's contribution to food security and sustainable agrifood systems.
Livestock supplies a third of global protein and roughly 40% of agricultural GDP (about USD 1.8 trillion) while
contributing 12% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, cattle the largest share and enteric methane a
major source; emission profiles differ by system, with low-external-input systems emitting less per unit area and
high-input systems less per kilogram of output. Relevant to transition risk in agricultural lending and insurance
books, and a counterweight to blanket sectoral exclusion approaches.
