occurrences.anchor_text: African Development Bank to back green hydrogen projects in Egypt, Morocco, Namibia and South Africa with grants worth a total of $20 million

report_fields.summary:
USD 20 million of reimbursable SEFA grants (board approval pending) across four projects — Project Ra in
Egypt (USD 3.55m, sustainable aviation fuels), Guelmim Green Hydrogen Valley in Morocco (USD 5.28m),
Hyphen in Namibia (USD 5.93m, marine fuels) and Saldanha Hydrogen DRI in South Africa (USD 5.24m, low-
carbon iron) — selected from 81 applications across 18 countries. Together they represent roughly USD 23
billion of total investment, 20 GW of renewable capacity, 7 GW of electrolysers and 2,950 MWh of storage: a
concrete read on the scale and construction-phase risk profile of African hydrogen build-out.

occurrences.anchor_text: CCRIF lifts parametric risk pool coverage another 14.5% to $1.8bn for current policy year

report_fields.summary:
CCRIF SPC's parametric risk pool has grown to USD 1.8 billion of coverage limits for the current policy year, up
14.5% on June 2026 and 25% on the prior year. Membership stands at 39, with four new members this season
— Jamaica Public Service Company, National Water Commission Jamaica, Nevis Electricity Company and
Nevis Water Department — all utilities, evidencing extension beyond sovereigns into water and electric utilities.
Since 2007 CCRIF has made 82 payouts totalling USD 483 million, disbursed within 14 days of a qualifying
event. The clearest sovereign-risk-pool datapoint of the window and a working example of parametric basis-risk
design at scale.

report_fields.summary:
Eight riparian states — Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe —
agreed priorities for a USD 130 million regional resilience programme with the Zambezi Watercourse
Commission, structured around natural resources management, community climate resilience, institutional
capacity and coordination, and recommending members allocate at least 10% of national budgets to programme
priorities. The basin supports over 380 million people dependent on hydropower, agriculture, fisheries and
drinking water, making it one of the most concentrated transboundary drought and hydrological risks on the
continent and a natural candidate for regional index-based risk transfer.

occurrences.anchor_text: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

report_fields.summary:
Documents a structural mismatch between policy incentive and buyer behaviour in the US voluntary market:
despite Section 45Q paying USD 180/t for direct air capture, DAC is only 2% of the largest US buyer's portfolio,
while biomass carbon removal and storage accounted for 96% of durable CDR purchase volume in 2025
(BECCS alone 69%). California's compliance programme has issued over 267 million offset credits through
2024, 81% from forest projects. The US CDR buyer base has doubled since 2022 to 69 buyers but average
purchase size has fallen — a thinning, not deepening, market.
report_fields.title: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

Global Center on Adaptation (GCA)
Website: gca.org
New roadmap signals Africa's pathway for sustainable and resilient agriculture
IN WINDOW 17 SEP 2026 REPORT ADAPTATION FINANCE
Marking ten years of the Initiative for the Adaptation of African Agriculture, FAO released The State of African
Agricultural Adaptation, 2016–2026: Assessment and Roadmap to 2036. Forty-six of 53 African countries have
costed combined adaptation needs of USD 566 billion across national plans — about USD 56 billion a year — of
which at least USD 80 billion is specifically agricultural, and that is a floor because 22 countries have not
itemised agriculture separately. This is the most usable denominator published this fortnight for African
adaptation protection-gap and sovereign-risk work.
📎  Source: FAO newsroom, 17 September 2026

A five-day technical workshop opening 14 September pre-validated Mozambique's updated National Strategy for
Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation (ENAMMC) to 2035, covering cyclones, floods, droughts and coastal
erosion, with an Action Plan, Resource Mobilisation Strategy and Communication Mechanism, funded through
AfDB's Africa NDC Hub and the Africa Climate Change Fund. Mozambique is among the most cyclone-exposed
economies in the world; the Resource Mobilisation Strategy is the document to which any future sovereign risk
transfer would be anchored.

Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS)
Website: ngfs.net
The most consequential supervisory publication of the fortnight. NGFS rewrote its supervisory guide for the first
time since May 2020, now placing nature-related financial risk on the same footing as climate and adding
transition planning, adaptation, stress-testing practice, litigation risk and disclosure. NGFS membership stands at
151 central banks and supervisors plus 24 observers.

The 2026 Status Report records over 1,000 organisations across 56 countries publishing TNFD-aligned
disclosures, a 100% year-on-year increase, with 802 committed Adopters and USD 26.6 trillion of AUM
represented by financial-institution adopters; 100 organisations have filed third-generation reports. Survey

now the baseline dataset for arguing nature-risk materiality to boards and supervisors.

occurrences.anchor_text: World Trade Report: Trade reform to boost growth; inaction can cost 10% global GDP

report_fields.summary:
The 2026 World Trade Report, launched at the opening of the Public Forum, finds a strengthened multilateral
trading system could increase global GDP by roughly 3% or USD 3 trillion by 2050, while failure to modernise
could reduce global output by up to 10%. Climate content is thin — the environmental transition is named as one
of the forces reshaping trade but the report is not structured around climate. Retained because the macro-
fragmentation assumptions feed directly into the narrative layer of transition scenarios, and because
fragmentation is the same mechanism that constrains cross-border reinsurance capacity.

report_fields.summary:
The Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter responding to feedback on its January 2026
consultation for a dedicated Parametric Special Purpose Insurer class supporting structured, fully collateralised
parametric risk transfer. The BMA will look to the substance of risk transfer rather than contractual form,
admitting contracts structured as reinsurance, derivatives or swaps provided statutory requirements are met;
existing SPIs may transition, and some may write both indemnity and parametric business case by case. An
amendment to the Insurance Act 1978 is being drafted for Q4 2026. The most consequential regulatory
development of the window for parametric and index-based climate covers.

report_fields.publisher: Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS)
report_fields.summary:
Surveys domestic tax treatment of agriculture and forestry across 89 countries including environmental tax
measures, and notes agriculture's role as a contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. Land-use and agricultural
taxation is the missing leg of most carbon-pricing coverage analysis, so this bears on anyone modelling the
forward path of carbon prices or agricultural transition risk — though climate is one objective among several here
rather than the organising frame.
Caveat. Partial verification. Title, paper number and authorship were read first-hand from the PDF cover, but IMF PDF
covers carry month only. The landing pages that would give the day are unreachable, so we cannot confirm this falls
inside 14–27 September rather than 5–13 September. Treat the date as September 2026.

occurrences.anchor_text: Extreme heat is breaking critical infrastructure. Can we adapt in time?

report_fields.summary:
Argues heat is now a correlated multi-system failure driver rather than an isolated peril: India lost an estimated
USD 78 billion, close to 2% of GDP, to heat in 2024, with outdoor workers losing nearly a tenth of annual
earnings, while Hungarian power demand rose 23% during last summer's heatwaves at the same time as
nuclear output fell on low Danube water levels. The compounding-correlation framing — grid, water and
hospitals failing together — is directly relevant to business-interruption accumulation and to scenario design.

occurrences.anchor_text: STATEMENT: US EPA Repeals Climate Pollution Rules for Power Plants

report_fields.summary:
EPA finalised a rule eliminating carbon emission limits on fossil-fuel-fired power plants, the sector responsible for
roughly a quarter of US climate pollution and its second-largest emissions source. WRI puts fossil electricity's
health toll at tens of thousands of avoidable impacts and hundreds of billions of dollars in health costs annually,
separate from climate-disaster costs averaging USD 150 billion a year. Following EPA's February 2026 reversal
of its own authority to limit climate pollution, this is a material transition-risk and litigation-risk data point for US
utility and energy exposures, and a concrete argument for reweighting away from rapid-transition scenarios in
US-centric books.

occurrences.anchor_text: Extreme heat is putting 2.4 billion workers at risk. Here's how 4 companies are responding

report_fields.summary:
WEF/BCG analysis: 2.4 billion workers, 70% of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat, with nearly
19,000 heat-linked worker deaths and 23 million injuries annually and projected productivity losses of USD 2.4
trillion a year by 2030. The implementation gap is the actuarially interesting number — 80% of companies name
extreme heat a business threat but only 28% have piloted interventions. Bayer reports a 20% reduction in heat-
related incidents in North America and USD 3,000 in avoided medical and lost-time costs per prevented claim, a
usable data point for workers' compensation and group health pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: Building Colombia's Nature Economy Could Create Hundreds of Thousands of New Jobs

report_fields.summary:
Estimates 775,000 jobs from nature tourism and agribusiness in Colombia by 2035 against a government-
identified pipeline of more than USD 32 billion in green investment opportunities. The transition-risk figure of note
is that about 4.7 million workers, roughly 22.6% of the current workforce, will be directly affected by the climate
transition, in a labour market where around 55% of workers were informally employed as of June 2026. A
concrete just-transition exposure quantification for an emerging-market sovereign, relevant both to sovereign
transition-risk scenarios and to life and health portfolios exposed to informal-sector displacement.

WRI's response to the UNSG Climate Summit, organised around keeping 1.5°C within reach, mobilising finance
for developing countries, and — new emphasis — advancing adaptation during climate overshoot. Germany
announced a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap to 2045; WRI cites a benefit-cost ratio of more than 10:1
over a decade for adaptation spending. The formal arrival of “adaptation under overshoot” in the multilateral
agenda is the signal for scenario designers: it legitimises planning around temporary exceedance of 1.5°C rather
than treating it as a tail case.

occurrences.anchor_text: ILS can play a broader role in narrowing the global protection gap: Moody's

report_fields.summary:
Moody's argues P&C insurers and reinsurers cannot close the protection gap alone given capital and regulatory
constraints, and positions insurance-linked securities as the marginal capacity source. Alternative capital
reached a record USD 147 billion in H1 2026; H1 2026 cat bond issuance set a record of nearly USD 18 billion;
outstanding cat bond market size was USD 65.6 billion at end-Q2 2026. Moody's cites Hurricane Melissa
(October 2025), which caused an estimated USD 12.2 billion of damage in Jamaica — 54% of GDP — and

Group of Twenty (G20)
Website: g20.org
The structural finding of this cycle. The 2026 United States presidency runs only four working groups — Trade,
Growth and Deregulation, Innovation, and Energy Abundance. There is no Sustainable Finance Working Group,
no climate or environment working group and no disaster risk reduction working group. The G20 climate and
sustainable finance workstream has effectively been stood down for 2026, and the Energy Abundance Ministerial
communiqué is the evidence.

Parag Khanna and WEF's Head of Climate Resilience argue the measurement barrier to adaptation finance has
been cleared — climate analytics now support credible avoided-loss quantification — yet mitigation still takes
over 90% of climate finance (USD 1.3 trillion in 2022) against roughly USD 68 billion a year for adaptation, and
only 9% of assessed companies are committing capital to adaptation against USD 1.47 trillion of identified
physical climate risk. The three proposed fixes (standardised resilience metrics, shared data architecture, and
market incentives including resilience-linked debt, blended finance and parametric triggers) map directly onto
actuarial territory.

report_fields.summary:
Sea level in much of the western tropical Pacific has risen 10–15 cm since 1993, close to or nearly twice the
global rate, yet only 15.6% of the combined land area of vulnerable atoll nations has LiDAR coverage, only about
three in ten residents of vulnerable coastal areas have ground measurements, and fewer than one in ten square
kilometres of nearshore reef and seabed has been surveyed at all. Tuvalu's 2019 survey captured roughly 500
km² of land, reef and lagoon in about 37 flying hours. Elevation and bathymetry data of this quality is the binding
constraint on credible SIDS flood and inundation models, and its absence is a first-order source of model
uncertainty in parametric and sovereign risk-pool pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: iClimateAction publishes three new reports on the climate observation data chain

report_fields.summary:
Three deliverables assessing the observational base underpinning climate services. In-situ networks supporting
the 55 Essential Climate Variables still depend heavily on short-term research projects, in-kind contributions or
volunteers, with material gaps across Africa, South America, Southeast Asia and the polar regions; satellite
observation covers 42 of the 55 ECVs, and a February 2026 survey of 33 climate experts found communication
with decision-makers, not data access or quality, the most-cited barrier to uptake. This is the observational-input
risk sitting underneath every catastrophe model and physical-risk scorecard — known geographic gaps and
funding fragility in the underlying networks are a source of parameter uncertainty that is rarely priced.

report_fields.summary:
A TNFD guide produced with UNEP FI, structured around ten questions for bank chief risk officers and risk
committees to test exposure to nature-related financial risk across credit and investment portfolios, with the
headline quantification that pollinator decline alone puts up to USD 577 billion of annual global crop production at
risk. It positions nature loss as a systemic financial-stability issue to be handled inside mainstream risk
frameworks rather than as a disclosure exercise, and is the bank-CRO companion to TNFD's earlier CFO and
asset-owner editions. Relevant to actuaries working on nature-related financial risk and on agricultural credit and
crop exposures.
Caveat. Partial verification. The UNEP FI landing page carries “September 2026” only and there is no matching item in
the UNEP FI news listing. Third-party coverage (Sustainable Japan, 18 September 2026) corroborates a release around
17–18 September but also states only the month. Title, URL, content and month are confirmed; the day is approximate.

## Registry article-version summary

The International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRI) at Columbia University reports that the equatorial Pacific is transitioning from declining La Nina conditions toward ENSO-neutral, with a 90% probability for March-May 2026. However, El Nino probabilities rise rapidly from May onward, reaching 72-80% by July-September 2026. For insurance and actuarial users, the IRI forecast provides critical forward-looking climate intelligence: the shift toward El Nino conditions in mid-2026 would alter tropical cyclone activity, drought, and flood risk patterns globally, requiring scenario updates in catastrophe models and catastrophe bond pricing.

A new WEF article (April 2026) examines how systemic risks — including climate change, cyber threats, and geopolitical instability — act as a hidden tax on economic growth, and how the insurance industry's expanding role can help build societal resilience before shocks occur. ## Registry article-version summary

The March 2026 ISSB update reveals a significant rebranding: the "BEES" (Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services) project has been officially renamed to "Nature-related Disclosures", expanding its scope beyond biodiversity to cover all natural-related risks and opportunities. The renamed project will serve as a targeted supplement to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, maintaining full compatibility with existing ISSB standards while aligning with TNFD, SASB, GRI, and ESRS frameworks to reduce duplicative corporate disclosures. ISSB discussed advancing the Nature-related Disclosures project toward a consultation draft, marking it as the next major standard-setting milestone after the IFRS S2 amendments.

Categories: climate-risk, insurance, catastrophe, finance-investment

## Verified article content

Natural disasters caused significant losses worldwide in 2025. All in all, damage amounting to some US$ 224bn was incurred, of which insurers covered around US$ 108bn. This means that 2025 joins a growing list of years with insured losses exceeding the US$ 100bn mark, despite losses being lower year on year. In 2024, inflation-adjusted overall losses had totalled US$ 368bn, of which US$ 147bn had been insured. Weather disasters accounted for 92% of all 2025 losses and for 97% of insured losses.

The Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter responding to feedback on its January 2026
consultation for a dedicated Parametric Special Purpose Insurer class supporting structured, fully collateralised
